To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

maize roots and leaves have distinct profiles of PYR/PIL/RCAR ARA receptor gene expression, and that the core ABA signaling pathway exhibits organ-, isoform-, and stress-specificity in response to abscisic Acid (ABA) or osmotic/dehydraion stress in maize seedlings.

the expression profiles of ABA receptor genes in response to A/B are distinct between maize roots and leaf, and that the ABA receptor gene family is involved in the regulation of ABA sensitivity in maize.

maize roots and leaves exhibit different transcriptional responses of the PYR/PYL ABA receptors and downstream core ABA signaling elements, and that this difference in gene expression is associated with distinct ABA sensitivity in roots versus leaves.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the organ-specific sensitivity to ABA between maize roots and shoots.

the transcriptional regulation of core ABA receptor gene family members, and the results provide novel insights into the perception of ABA and its signaling pathways in the roots and leaves of maize seedlings.

the organ-specific and stimulus-dependent transcriptional response of the PYR1/PYR/PYL/ RCAR ABA receptors in roots and leaves of maize seedlings, which may contribute to our understanding of the molecular mechanisms of ABA perception and signal transduction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the transcriptional responses of the PYR/PYL ABA receptor genes in maize roots and leaves to ABA or stress are different, and the different responses of the PYLs to ABA or water stress are organ-specific.
the ABA signal transduction network in maize leaves and roots is differentially regulated by ABA or stress-induced endogenous abscisic acids.
ABA signaling is organ-specific, and that the perception of ABA is organ- and species-specific.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the different actions of ABA in the aboveground versus belowground parts of the plant are due to a distinct perception mechanism in the leaves and roots.

the transcriptional regulation of PYR1/ PYL/RCAR AIBA receptors is organ-specific, and the expression profiles of core signaling components in response ABA or dehydration are distinct between maize leaves and roots.
the ABA perception and transduction machinery is differentially regulated in maize leaves and roots.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transcriptional responses of core ABA signal components are different between roots and leaves, and between ABA and osmotic/dehydration stresses, and this is the first report on this subject.
the ABA signaling components are not only differentially expressed in response to A
the ABA signaling network in roots is much more sensitive to ABA than that in leaves, which is consistent with the fact that ABA is a root-to-shoot signal in plants.
